Promo / Hype Seller
Your style: tone reference only (your best past hook): "Get the best dental care with the brand new" (Bold / Shocking Claim). Match the energy, not the words.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): one bold, true claim
One extreme or contrarian line that is true for the product. Example shapes: "Stop brushing like this." / "You'll never use a weed wacker again."
No deal is live: skip urgency lines.
Swing option: a bold claim that withholds the answer, e.g. "Stop buying a new toothbrush. Here's why."

## Beats
1. **3-10 s:** prove the claim on screen right away (demo or a number on screen). Proof to show: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds.
2. **10-20 s:** why it matters and who it's for. Keep cuts fast.
3. **20-30 s:** link and CTA: tap the basket.

## Avoid
- Vague claims ("best ever") with no proof on screen.
- A deal with no reason to care about the product first.
- Opening with social proof only ("this changed our routine"). It tends to underperform.

Relatable Parent

Relatable Parent

## Hook (first 3 seconds): a question that names the pain
Open by asking the viewer about the struggle, in your own words. Example shape: "Does your kid fight you every night over brushing?"
Do not open with "So yesterday..." and do not say the product name yet.
Swing option: a curiosity opener told as a story, e.g. "I found out why my kid suddenly asks to brush."

1. **3-8 s:** one real moment from your house (the fight, the tears). Your words, one detail.
2. **8-20 s:** show Autobrush Sonic Pro Kids Bundle in use on your kid. Show this one claim, don't list it: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds.
3. **20-30 s:** the result in your words ("now she asks for it"). One concrete detail beats "it's great".
4. **CTA:** one line: tap the basket.

## Avoid
- More than one pain in the opening line.
- Reading specs (ADA-accepted U-shaped design, music + LED lights make kids want to brush) to camera. Show them.

# Content brief for @somo.mama: Autobrush Sonic Pro Kids Bundle
Relatable Parent
Your style: tone reference only (your best past hook): "1) try an expensive toothbrush? Or 2) have an" (Direct Question). Match the energy, not the words.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): a question that names the pain
Open by asking the viewer about the struggle, in your own words. Example shape: "Does your kid fight you every night over brushing?"
Do not open with "So yesterday..." and do not say the product name yet.
Swing option: a curiosity opener told as a story, e.g. "I found out why my kid suddenly asks to brush."

## Beats
1. **3-8 s:** one real moment from your house (the fight, the tears). Your words, one detail.
2. **8-20 s:** show Autobrush Sonic Pro Kids Bundle in use on your kid. Show this one claim, don't list it: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds.
3. **20-30 s:** the result in your words ("now she asks for it"). One concrete detail beats "it's great".
4. **CTA:** one line: tap the basket.

## Avoid
- More than one pain in the opening line.
- Reading specs (ADA-accepted U-shaped design, music + LED lights make kids want to brush) to camera. Show them.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): one bold, true claim

# Content brief for @found.it.first: Autobrush Sonic Pro Kids Bundle
Promo / Hype Seller
Your style: tone reference only (your best past hook): "Great Deal" (Offer / Urgency). Match the energy, not the words.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): one bold, true claim
One extreme or contrarian line that is true for the product. Example shapes: "Stop brushing like this." / "You'll never use a weed wacker again."
No deal is live: skip urgency lines.
Swing option: a bold claim that withholds the answer, e.g. "Stop buying a new toothbrush. Here's why."

## Beats
1. **3-10 s:** prove the claim on screen right away (demo or a number on screen). Proof to show: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds.
2. **10-20 s:** why it matters and who it's for. Keep cuts fast.
3. **20-30 s:** link and CTA: tap the basket.

## Avoid
- Vague claims ("best ever") with no proof on screen.
- A deal with no reason to care about the product first.
- Opening with social proof only ("this changed our routine"). It tends to underperform.

brief:
# Content brief for @jaymee.lynne: Autobrush Sonic Pro Kids Bundle
Relatable Parent
Your style: tone reference only (your best past hook): "Perfect for your lazy kids who don’t love brushing" (Problem / Pain Point). Match the energy, not the words.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): a question that names the pain
Open by asking the viewer about the struggle, in your own words. Example shape: "Does your kid fight you every night over brushing?"
Do not open with "So yesterday..." and do not say the product name yet.
Swing option: a curiosity opener told as a story, e.g. "I found out why my kid suddenly asks to brush."

## Beats
1. **3-8 s:** one real moment from your house (the fight, the tears). Your words, one detail.
2. **8-20 s:** show Autobrush Sonic Pro Kids Bundle in use on your kid. Show this one claim, don't list it: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds.
3. **20-30 s:** the result in your words ("now she asks for it"). One concrete detail beats "it's great".
4. **CTA:** one line: tap the basket.

## Avoid
- More than one pain in the opening line.
- Reading specs (ADA-accepted U-shaped design, music + LED lights make kids want to brush) to camera. Show them.

Show-and-Tell / Reveal
Your style: no clear past hook found; use your natural voice.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): a visible action, result hidden
Do something physical with the product on camera and withhold the result. Example shapes: "Watch what happens when I click this." / "Wait until you see what this does."
Product in frame, result not shown yet. No product name in the first line.
Swing option: tease the result with "nobody tells you" or "wait for it" before the reveal.

## Beats
1. **3-10 s:** reveal the result. The loop must close within 10 seconds.
2. **10-25 s:** demo one benefit by showing it: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds. A plain, clean demo is a safe fallback.

Promo / Hype Seller
Your style: tone reference only (your best past hook): "Guys this sale is insane 🤯🤯" (Offer / Urgency). Match the energy, not the words.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): one bold, true claim
One extreme or contrarian line that is true for the product. Example shapes: "Stop brushing like this." / "You'll never use a weed wacker again."
No deal is live: skip urgency lines.
Swing option: a bold claim that withholds the answer, e.g. "Stop buying a new toothbrush. Here's why."

## Beats
1. **3-10 s:** prove the claim on screen right away (demo or a number on screen). Proof to show: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds.
2. **10-20 s:** why it matters and who it's for. Keep cuts fast.
3. **20-30 s:** link and CTA: tap the basket.

## Avoid
- Vague claims ("best ever") with no proof on screen.
- A deal with no reason to care about the product first.
- Opening with social proof only ("this changed our routine"). It tends to underperform.

# Content brief for @devsbodega: Autobrush Sonic Pro Kids Bundle
Promo / Hype Seller
Your style: tone reference only (your best past hook): "My girl says all she needs is 30 seconds." (Social Proof / Results). Match the energy, not the words.

## Hook (first 3 seconds): one bold, true claim
One extreme or contrarian line that is true for the product. Example shapes: "Stop brushing like this." / "You'll never use a weed wacker again."
No deal is live: skip urgency lines.
Swing option: a bold claim that withholds the answer, e.g. "Stop buying a new toothbrush. Here's why."

## Beats
1. **3-10 s:** prove the claim on screen right away (demo or a number on screen). Proof to show: full-mouth clean in 30 seconds.
2. **10-20 s:** why it matters and who it's for. Keep cuts fast.
3. **20-30 s:** link and CTA: tap the basket.

## Avoid
- Vague claims ("best ever") with no proof on screen.
- A deal with no reason to care about the product first.
- Opening with social proof only ("this changed our routine"). It tends to underperform.
